page_title: App Vanish: free Mac app uninstaller

sources.entry: App Vanish - Drop an app on the bin to remove it and the files it left behind. Unsure files start unticked and everything goes to the Trash. The App Store edition finds leftovers of apps you already deleted. summary.name: App Vanish
summary.one_liner: A free Mac app uninstaller that removes an app along with the leftover files it left across your Library, moving everything to the Trash.
use_cases: Completely removing a Mac app and its support files
Finding leftover files from apps already deleted
Cleaning up LaunchAgents and helper apps left behind
Reviewing uninstall candidates before removing them
Installing a free uninstaller via Homebrew
summary.what_it_does: App Vanish removes a Mac app by dragging it onto the bin or choosing it from a file picker. It reads the app's identity and searches common Library locations such as Application Support, Preferences, Caches, Logs, Containers, Group Containers, cookies and web data, LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons, privileged helpers, install receipts and helper apps. It shows every file found with its size and location, and unsure files start unticked. Ticked files move to the Trash so they can be restored. The Mac App Store edition cannot remove apps itself, but it finds leftovers of apps already moved to the Trash.
notable: Unsure files start unticked and everything goes to the Trash
Mac App Store edition finds leftovers of apps already deleted, running in App Sandbox
Signed and notarized by Apple; open source under MIT license on GitHub
Asks apps to quit rather than force quitting them; refuses Apple system apps
caveats: The App Store edition cannot remove apps itself; it only cleans leftovers after you trash an app
Only covers the listed Library locations, so some files may not be found
Requires macOS; no Windows or Linux version named
